title: Drop the Price From 1 Cent to Free — and Demand Jumps From 27% to 69%

segments.text: Drop the price from 1 cent to free — and demand jumps from 27% to 69%. Same product. Different brain.
69% Chose the Free Item vs 27% at 1¢
segments.narration: MIT researchers dropped the price of a Hershey Kiss from one cent to zero. Demand jumped from 27 percent to 69 percent. Same product, same relative value — the brain treats free as a completely different category.

segments.text: 73% of Amazon Prime Trials Convert to Paid
segments.narration: Amazon's free trial converts roughly 73 percent of users to paid subscribers. The industry average for software free trials is around 20 percent. The gap comes from delivering real value during the trial, not just a limited demo.

Costco's in-store sampling consistently produces two to four times normal sales on sampled items. Remove the risk of a bad purchase, let the product speak for itself, and conversion follows at a rate no advertisement can match.

segments.title: % Who Chose the Hershey Kiss — MIT Cafeteria Experiment
segments.narration: When the Kiss dropped from one cent to free, the share choosing it more than doubled — from 27 to 69 percent. The truffle was still a better deal on paper. Free overrides the rational calculation entirely.
